meta.title: Addiction Risk Self-Screen
meta.description: A non-diagnostic 500-question self-screen across 20 addiction-risk and recovery dimensions.

levels.label: Very High Current Concern
levels.desc: Your responses indicate many serious warning signs. Please seek prompt assessment from a qualified addiction or healthcare professional. Do not stop alcohol, benzodiazepines, or another dependence-forming substance suddenly without medical advice.

levels.label: High Current Concern
levels.desc: Your responses indicate substantial loss of control or harm. A timely confidential professional assessment and support plan are strongly recommended.

levels.label: Elevated Current Concern
levels.desc: Several meaningful warning signs are present. Consider discussing them soon with a qualified healthcare or addiction professional.

levels.label: Moderate Current Concern
levels.desc: Some patterns may be affecting safety, wellbeing, or responsibilities. Early support can help clarify risk and prevent escalation.

levels.label: Some Warning Signs
levels.desc: A smaller number of warning signs appear present. Pay attention to changes, consequences, and difficulty controlling the pattern; seek help if concerned.

levels.label: Lower Current Concern — Not No Risk
levels.desc: Fewer warning signs were endorsed, but this does not rule out risk or a disorder. Any overdose, dangerous withdrawal, or serious consequence needs professional attention.
